long_biography.plain_text:
Abramovich's business path began in commodity trading before post-Soviet privatisation opened a decisive route into oil. He and partners acquired control of Sibneft in the mid-1990s, then sold the controlling stake to Gazprom in 2005. The sale converted an operating oil holding into investment capital, and his portfolio expanded into steel and nickel.

Chukotka gave the career an unusual public chapter. Abramovich served as governor of the remote Russian region for eight years and directed substantial investment there. Football later made him internationally familiar: he bought Chelsea Football Club and owned it for nearly two decades, describing the sport's unpredictability as the attraction that drew him in.
